editorial:
The Painted Stallion is a 12-chapter Republic Pictures serial released June 5, 1937. It was directed by Alan James, Ray Taylor and William Witney. Ray "Crash" Corrigan stars as Clark Stuart, with Hoot Gibson, LeRoy Mason and Duncan Renaldo. Hal Taliaferro and Jack Perrin play Jim Bowie and Davy Crockett. Republic cut the serial into a 67-minute feature, released February 11, 1938. A creator would want it for the Western serial footage and the frontier-figure cameos.

The rights trap is the renewal record. As a 1937 film its first term ran 28 years, so any renewal would fall in 1964 to 1966. A text scan of the Catalog of Copyright Entries volumes for those years found no listing. That scan was not a page-by-page read, and the Copyright Office public-records search was not completed. Until both are done, treat the print as unconfirmed. Do not assume the 1938 feature cut or the 2005 Alpha Video DVD share the serial's status.
faq: Can I use The Painted Stallion in my own project?

Not yet with confidence. A text scan of the 1964 to 1966 Catalog of Copyright Entries found no renewal. The Copyright Office public records, which cover filings from 1978 on, have not been searched. Run that search first. A repeat of the volume check by hand would also help.
Does the Internet Archive upload mean the film is free to reuse?
No. The Internet Archive item is a user upload, and hosting a film there is not a rights finding. Use it to watch the serial. Settle the renewal question before you reuse any footage.
